key_concepts: Plants reproduce sexually through flowers and seeds.
Flower parts include petals, sepals, stamen, and pistil.
The stamen is the male reproductive part that produces pollen.
The pistil is the female reproductive part that contains ovules.
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the stamen to the pistil.
Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant.
Pollinators such as bees and butterflies help transfer pollen.
Wind and rain can affect pollination success.
Fertilization after pollination leads to seed production.
Plants can also reproduce asexually without seeds or flowers.
Asexual reproduction includes vegetative propagation by runners, tubers, and cuttings.
